The fourth-century quarters had residential and religious structures, including a basilica-style church in the Dakhla oasis. Archaeologists also found coins, pottery fragments and tools.

The ​birth of these endangered big cats – including an exceedingly rare white tiger – has revitalised a team of zoo workers, he said.

Interim president says unrest will not break out despite anger at official response to the 24 June disaster

Venezuela’s interim president has defended her country’s emergency response to the twin earthquakes that have killed more than 3,000 people, vowing the country would not descend into social unrest.

Many Venezuelans have expressed anger at what they see as the US-backed government’s inadequate response to the 24 June disaster before international teams arrived.

rfi.description: The Paris court of appeal is to rule Tuesday afternoon in far right leader Marine Le Pen’s embezzlement case, in a decision that could determine whether she can run for president for a fourth time, or if she will step aside. Several scenarios are possible, and her political opponents are preparing for all possibilities.

rfi.description: As NATO leaders gather in Ankara tomorrow, Tuesday, the alliance faces a stark test of unity, burden-sharing and strategic clarity, with the war in Ukraine, transatlantic tensions and Middle East instability all pressing heavily on the agenda.

rfi.title: France's first diagnosed Ebola patient recovers after treatment
rfi.description: A French doctor who was the first-ever diagnosed case of Ebola in the country has made a full recovery and has been discharged from hospital.

rfi.title: Major wildfires burn in Southern France as early fire season hits Europe
rfi.description: Firefighters are fighting wildfires across southern France and other parts of Europe, and authorities are warning that this year’s fire season has started a month earlier than usual after early heatwaves in May and June left vegetation particularly dry and vulnerable.

rfi.title: Macron to become first Western European leader to visit post-Assad Syria
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron ​will visit ‌Syria to discuss ways to ​strengthen bilateral ​relations and issues of ⁠mutual interest, ​the Syrian presidency has announced, in what would be the first visit by a Western European head of state since Ahmed al-Sharaa came to power following the overthrow of Bashar al-Assad in late 2024.

rfi.title: Merino's late strike takes Spain past Portugal into World Cup quarter-finals
rfi.description: Mikel Merino scored in second half stoppage time at the Dallas Stadium on Monday to send Spain past Portugal into the last eight at the 2026 World Cup and end the World Cup career of Portugal skipper Cristiano Ronaldo.

rfi.title: Rebels seize key town of Anéfis as they tighten grip on northern Mali
rfi.description: Tuareg separatists and al-Qaeda affiliates appear to have secured control of a key town in northern Mali following a coordinated offensive by the rebels over the weekend. The Malian army and Russian mercenaries have been holed up in the key camp of Anéfis after the rebels launched their offensive on Saturday.

rfi.title: Tour de France bans spectators from third stage as fire burns in French Pyrenees
rfi.description: Spectators have been banned from the third stage of the Tour de France cycling race through the Pyrenees Monday, which will be adapted as a forest fire burns the area.

rfi.title: Facing heavy security, Tanzania protesters fear repeat of election violence
rfi.description: Tanzanians planning to protest on Tuesday against government repression are facing a heavy police presence and warnings from authorities, which recalls the mass killings that followed last October's disputed election.

rfi.title: England survive Azteca thriller to set up last eight showdown with Norway
rfi.description: England moved into a last eight clash with Norway after they beat Mexico 3-2 in a whirlwind game for the ages at the Estadio Azteca in Mexico City.

rfi.title: Haaland's late strikes take Norway past Brazil to last eight for first time
rfi.description: Erling Haaland scored twice in the last 11 minutes to sweep Norway past Brazil into the World Cup quarter-finals for the first time.

rfi.title: Summit host Turkey eyes major weapons deals with NATO allies
rfi.description: Next week's NATO Summit in Ankara is expected to showcase Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s rising influence within the alliance, as he aims to use the gathering to overcome resistance to crucial arms deals and highlight the rapid growth of Turkey’s defence industry.

rfi.title: Three sons of Iran's slain leader Khamenei appear at funeral, not successor Mojtaba
rfi.description: Three sons of slain Iranian leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei prayed beside his coffin and those of four other family members on Sunday, but Mojtaba, the son who has succeeded him as Iran's supreme leader, ​did not make ‌an appearance.

euronews.title: Woman wanted for Monaco bomb attack found dead in Ukraine, local police say
euronews.description: The announcement comes after authorities across Europe were hunting for the woman suspected of planting a bomb in Monaco that wounded three people, including a Ukrainian-born tycoon and his teenaged son.

euronews.title: Hyperion GR-1 enters orbit: A new step for Greece's space programme
euronews.description: It is the first Greek optical microsatellite developed under the National Microsatellite Programme - launched from Cape Canaveral.

euronews.title: Parkout, the app connecting drivers to parking spaces in Athens
euronews.description: It operates in Athens districts without controlled parking, outside the historic centre, and lets drivers signal a freed space so a nearby motorist can claim it.

euronews.title: Is Google using your searches to train its AI? Here's how to opt out
euronews.description: The changes reflect a broader industry shift. Rather than relying solely on data scraped from the web, companies are increasingly mining people's everyday interactions with digital services.

euronews.title: European Parliament approves free cabin luggage and new delay compensation rules for air passengers
euronews.description: Lawmakers gave the final green light to the revised regulation after a decade of talks with EU countries. Airlines argue the new rules will inevitably lead to higher ticket prices. Passenger associations say rights have been upheld.

euronews.title: 'Portugal is an energy island and needs more flexibility,' minister says
euronews.description: The Portuguese government argues that because limited connections isolate Iberia from the European grid, the country faces many of the same challenges as the EU's outermost regions and deserves compensation for the lack of interconnections.

euronews.title: European Parliament to ask for probe into FIFA boss Infantino over Balogun red card

euronews.title: US President Donald Trump arrives in Turkey to attend NATO summit
euronews.description: The two-day gathering in Ankara comes a year after NATO members pledged to ramp up security-related spending to 5% of GDP under pressure from the US leader. Yet, the US President has lashed out at European allies over Iran.

euronews.title: Dustin Hoffman and Maggie Gyllenhaal honoured at Karlovy Vary Film Festival opening ceremony
euronews.description: The 60th Karlovy Vary International Film Festival opened with a star-studded ceremony, welcoming Hollywood names including Dustin Hoffman, Maggie Gyllenhaal, Harvey Keitel and Jesse Eisenberg.

euronews.title: Scientists find new way to fight antibiotic-resistant bacteria
euronews.description: The study involving Pompeu Fabra University identifies a mechanism to strip bacteria of protection in the lab, opening new ways to fight antibiotic resistance.

euronews.title: South Korean law targeting 'fake news' takes effect as journalists' groups raise concerns
euronews.description: South Korea saw a surge in online misinformation following the botched 2024 martial law attempt, including unsubstantiated allegations of Chinese interference in the electoral system.

euronews.title: Has online shopping from outside the EU become more expensive?
euronews.description: Several social media users are claiming that online shopping has become more expensive because of a new EU import charge. The Cube takes a look.

euronews.title: Dubai's new startup campus wants to be the front door for founders
euronews.description: Backed by Dubai’s D33 agenda, Dubai Founders HQ connects founders with investors, corporates and government to speed ideas from launch to growth.

euronews.title: ‘Overturn this’: Belgium mocks Donald Trump and FIFA with dance and post after victory against US
euronews.description: Belgium has ended the USA’s World Cup campaign, with many taking great joy in the host nation’s humiliating 4-1 defeat following the controversy over FIFA’s decision to suspend a US red card prior to the game.

euronews.title: Macron tours Damascus' Umayyad Mosque during Syria visit
euronews.description: French President Emmanuel Macron visits Damascus' Umayyad Mosque with Syrian leader Ahmed al-Sharaa and signs the guestbook during his Syria trip.

euronews.title: Euro area 'under strain' as recession risks loom
euronews.description: Rolf R. Strauch, Chief Economist at the European Stability Mechanism, said governments "have to create growth" to avoid a possible recession. The global instability poses "high demands" in governments that have to face them with limited fiscal space.

euronews.title: Nothing beats a Jet2 holiday, but what about a Jet2 wedding?
euronews.description: Planning a wedding in Europe can be a lot to organise, but now Jet2 has added new destinations for the big day, including Malta, Italy, Greece, Spain, Türkiye and Portugal.

euronews.title: Samsung loses over $100bn in market value despite record AI-driven profit
euronews.description: Samsung Electronics has forecast a nineteen-fold leap in quarterly profit, its third record quarter in a row, yet investors responded by wiping more than $100 billion (€87.5bn) off the company's value amid doubts over how long the AI-driven memory boom can last.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, procès en appel de Marine Le Pen : suivez la lecture de l’arrêt devant la cour d’appel de Paris
lemonde.description: Le parquet général a requis, dans ce procès des assistants parlementaires européens du FN, quatre ans de prison, dont un an ferme, et cinq ans d’inéligibilité sans exécution provisoire contre Marine Le Pen. La décision de la cour d’appel sera décisive pour l’avenir politique de la cheffe de file des députés du RN.

lemonde.title: Canicule : à Paris, le réseau électrique d’Enedis face à « des accumulations de chaleur inédites »

lemonde.title: En Cisjordanie, une « annexion de facto à un rythme sans précédent » : le rapport alarmant de deux ONG israéliennes
lemonde.description: Israël contrôle désormais 18 % des territoires occupés, contre 7 % avant la guerre à Gaza. Un rapport des ONG Peace Now et Kerem Navot documente l’accélération, depuis trois ans et demi, de l’accaparement des terres, de la construction de routes réservées aux colons et des expulsions de communautés locales.

lemonde.title: Explosions à Damas : Emmanuel Macron avait quitté le quartier de son hôtel ; 18 blessés selon le ministère de l’intérieur
lemonde.description: Des témoins ont vu de la fumée s’élever d’un secteur proche de l’hôtel où le président français a passé la nuit, dans le centre de la capitale syrienne, qu’il a quitté mardi matin pour des entretiens au palais présidentiel.

lemonde.title: « Mauvais karma, M. le président » : la presse étrangère tance Donald Trump après l’élimination des Etats-Unis par la Belgique en Coupe du monde
lemonde.description: Balayée lundi en huitièmes de finale du tournoi, la Team USA n’a pas profité de la présence sur le terrain de Folarin Balogun, dont la suspension avait été levée après l’intervention du président américain auprès du patron de la FIFA.

lemonde.title: Le cycle menstruel, une fenêtre sur la santé des femmes à exploiter

lemonde.description: Anastasiia Berezovska a été retrouvée sans vie en Ukraine avec « des blessures par balle à la tête », a annoncé mardi la police nationale ukrainienne, qui a arrêté deux suspects.

lemonde.title: En Hongrie, Péter Magyar lance une procédure contestée pour destituer le président
lemonde.description: Le Parlement hongrois examine à partir de mardi 7 juillet un paquet d’amendements constitutionnels prévoyant la destitution du président Tamas Sulyok, proche de l’ex-premier ministre Viktor Orban. lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, Tour de France : suivez la quatrième étape, entre Carcassonne et Foix
lemonde.description: Les coureurs de la Grande Boucle découvrent, mardi, un parcours entièrement sur le territoire français, pour la première fois dans cette 113ᵉ édition.

lemonde.title: OTAN : une série de annoncés à Ankara, dont un pour Airbus
lemonde.description: Les pays de l’OTAN se réunissent mardi et mercredi lors d’un sommet à Ankara, destiné à démontrer l’engagement des alliés européens à développer leurs capacités de défense, comme le réclament les Etats-Unis de Donald Trump.

lemonde.description: Ces nouvelles mises en examen portent leur nombre total à 11. Tué en novembre 2025 à Marseille, Mehdi Kessaci était le frère d’Amine Kessaci, une figure de la lutte contre le narcotrafic.

lemonde.title: A Nîmes, le nouveau maire communiste Vincent Bouget met la gauche en pratique
lemonde.description: Concertation citoyenne, dialogue avec les agents, gratuité des bibliothèques… Après vingt-cinq ans de gestion par la droite, l’élu de 46 ans tente d’incarner une rupture tant symbolique que politique.

lemonde.title: A Barcelone, les architectes au chevet d’une planète en transition
lemonde.description: Les débats thématiques du congrès de l’Union internationale des architectes ont balayé le spectre des crises auxquelles la discipline doit se confronter. Une grande exposition leur faisait écho, ainsi qu’une série de projets de recherche.

france24fr.title: Burkina Faso : la France retire tous ses diplomates après la rupture des relations
france24fr.description: Tous les diplomates français en poste au Burkina Faso sont rentrés en France "en fin de semaine dernière" et le personnel diplomatique du Burkina doit quitter la France d'ici lundi soir, a indiqué lundi à l'AFP le ministère français des Affaires étrangères.

france24fr.title: Colis piégé à Monaco : l'Ukrainienne suspectée a été retrouvée morte près de Kiev
france24fr.description: Le corps d'Anastasia Berezovska, la ⁠femme ukrainienne soupçonnée d'avoir ​déposé un colis piégé à Monaco la semainedernière, a été retrouvé sans vie ​près de Kiev, selon un média local. Une information confirmée notamment par le bureau du procureur général ukrainien, qui précise que la femme est morte par balle.

france24fr.title: Burkina Faso : la France retire ses diplomates après la rupture annoncée par Ouaga
france24fr.description: Le personnel diplomatique du Burkina Faso devrait quitter la France ce lundi soir. Une mesure qui intervient une semaine après la décision unilatérale des autorités burkinabè de rompre les relations diplomatiques avec Paris. La France annonce également le retour dans l'hexagone de tous ses diplomates en provenance du Burkina Faso.

france24fr.title: Narcotrafic : quatre autres suspects écroués pour le "meurtre en bande organisée" de Mehdi Kessaci
france24fr.description: Quatre nouveaux suspects ont été mis en examen notamment pour "meurtre et tentative de meurtre en bande organisée". Ils ont été écroués dans le cadre de l'enquête sur le meurtre à Marseille du frère d'Amine Kessaci, militant écologiste engagé dans la lutte contre le narcotrafic. L'assassinat de Mehdi Kessaci avait provoqué une onde de choc.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : la Belgique a su se faire "justice" après l'affaire du carton rouge de Balogun
france24fr.description: Remontée après le scandale Balogun, la Belgique a sorti sèchement les l'équipe des États-Unis dès les 8es de finale de leur propre Mondial. Les joueurs belges n'ont pas manqué de se rappeler sur le terrain au bon souvenir du président américain Trump, en imitant notamment sa danse à l'issue du dernier but de la rencontre.

france24fr.title: Syrie : Emmanuel Macron maintient sa visite malgré deux explosions à Damas
france24fr.description: Deux bombes ont explosé mardi matin à Damas à proximité de l'hôtel où ​Emmanuel Macron venait d'échanger avec des acteurs de la société civile, ont rapporté les médias officiels syriens, mais le président français, qui avait quitté les lieux peu avant, est indemne et entend maintenir ​le programme ‌de sa visite, selon l'Elysée.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : Mohamed Salah, le Pharaon qui inscrit les Égyptiens dans l'Histoire du football
france24fr.description: Mohamed Salah emmène mardi soir ses coéquipiers vers l'Histoire. Pour la première fois, l'Égypte s'est qualifiée en phase à élimination directe. Face à l'Argentine de Léo Messi à 18 heures, le capitaine égyptien n'a plus rien à prouver dans sa carrière internationale.

france24fr.title: Syrie : la reconstruction attire les entreprises françaises
france24fr.description: Une double explosion près de l'hôtel où séjournait Emmanuel Macron est venue perturber la visite du président français à Damas. Mais le programme a été maintenu, en particulier le forum d'affaires franco-syrien. Derrière le rapprochement diplomatique entre la France et la Syrie, Paris espère prendre pied sur un marché de la reconstruction estimé à plus de 216 milliards de dollars. Mais entre concurrence des pays du Golfe, sanctions encore en vigueur et instabilité politique, les obstacles resten

france24fr.title: Maia Sandu et l'Union européenne : l'ombre de la désinformation russe
france24fr.description: En Moldavie, il existe un dynamisme politique vers l'Occident, mais pas forcément une stabilité face aux influences extérieures.

france24fr.title: Menace russe, Groenland : au Danemark, la lutte contre les fausses informations
france24fr.description: Face aux pressions américaines concernant le Groenland et à la menace russe à l'est, le Danemark a fait de la défense européenne une priorité. De nombreuses fausses informations circulent sur Internet pour diviser le pays à ce sujet, mais des efforts sont déployés pour les contrer.

france24fr.title: Colère agricole : quand l'infox s'invite dans les champs
france24fr.description: En Europe, il existe un dynamisme des mouvements sociaux, mais pas forcément une véracité des images partagées.

france24fr.title: Les leçons oubliées de la crise de 2008 : le crédit privé, une bombe financière ?
france24fr.description: Sommes-nous à la veille d'une crise financière mondiale ? Une crise qui ne viendrait pas forcément de la bulle IA, mais du crédit privé, un pan de la finance de l'ombre : ces fonds qui prêtent aux entreprises délaissées par les banques traditionnelles. Or ces fonds sont fragilisés, car les entreprises ne parviennent plus à rembourser. Faut-il s'en inquiéter ?

france24fr.title: Délibéré du procès Le Pen : une décision décisive pour son avenir politique
france24fr.description: Marine Le Pen pourrait être confrontée à une incertitude selon la décision que rendra mardi après-midi la cour d'appel de Paris, tant plusieurs points juridiques demeurent sujets à caution.

france24fr.title: Attentats à la bombe : Emmanuel Macron sain et sauf, sa visite se poursuit (Elysée)
france24fr.description: Le président français Emmanuel Macron est sain et sauf et poursuit sa visite en Syrie, a assuré mardi l'Elysée après l'explosion de deux bombes à proximité de l'hôtel où il a passé la nuit dans le centre de Damas.

france24fr.title: 14 juillet 2016 : la nuit qui a brisé Nice
france24fr.description: Le 14 juillet 2016, Nice est frappée par l'attentat le plus meurtrier de son histoire, revendiqué par l'organisation Etat islamique (EI). Un camion bélier fait irruption sur la promenade des Anglais et fauche les spectateurs rassemblés par dizaines de milliers pour assister au feu d'artifices de la fête nationale. Le terroriste tue 86 personnes et en blesse des centaines d'autres. Dix ans plus tard, nos équipes sont retournées sur les lieux du drame à la rencontre des victimes.

france24fr.title: En Allemagne, l'armée attire les jeunes
france24fr.description: L'Allemagne réarme, alors que son économie se contracte, avec des milliers de suppressions de postes dans l’industrie et les services. Dans ce contexte, la Bundeswehr est devenue, presque par défaut, l'un des employeurs les plus attractifs du pays pour les jeunes : les candidatures ont bondi de 23% en janvier 2026. Mais derrière ces chiffres se cache une réalité : pour beaucoup de jeunes Allemands, l'uniforme n'est pas un idéal, c'est un plan B. Reportage d'Anne Mailliet.

france24fr.title: Collections mode masculine printemps-été 2027, la planète brûle
france24fr.description: Alors que, dans plusieurs pays, la liberté d’expression est menacée par la montée du populisme, les designers ne peuvent plus se voiler la face. Yohji Yamamoto s’insurge, ses vêtements sont comme brûlés par le soleil. Issey Miyake exalte l’ombre des bambous, Jeanne Friot accuse les politiques, l’IFM exhorte ses étudiants à repousser les limites, KML, la griffe d’origine saoudienne, tourne en dérision les codes vestimentaires de l’Occident. Et toutes et tous de s’interroger, quelles propositions

zeit.title: Härtefälle: 30 Geflüchtete dürfen vorerst in Sachsen-Anhalt bleiben
Illegale Waffengeschäfte: Jahre nach Urteil: Heckler & Koch tätigt Mexiko-Strafzahlung
Nato-Gipfel in Ankara: USA und Europa vereinbaren gemeinsame Produktion von Raketen
zeit.description: Die Nato-Länder wollen gemeinsam Lenkwaffen und Abwehrraketen bauen und warten. Rheinmetall und Lockheed Martin vereinbaren Herstellung taktischer Raketen in Deutschland.

zeit.title: A3 in Unterfranken: Wohnmobil fängt während Fahrt Feuer - Fahrer verletzt
Heino möchte Zeichen setzen: Nach AfD-Post: Heino will 30.000 Euro - mindestens
Drogen und Sucht: 2.150 Drogentote - Jeder vierte unter 30 Jahre
Wasserversorgung: Wasserrohrbruch spült Sand auf Straße – lange Reparatur
Marineschiffbau: So läuft der U-Boot-Deal mit Kanada
Kirchensteuer der katholischen Kirche: Katholische Kirche nehmen 2025 mehr Kirchensteuern ein
zeit.description: Die katholischen Bistümer haben trotz weniger Mitglieder mehr Kirchensteuern eingenommen als im Vorjahr. Wegen der Inflation verringerte sich jedoch die Kaufkraft.

zeit.title: Europäische Union: EU-Parlament stimmt für Prüfverfahren gegen Parteifamilie der AfD
zeit.description: Eine EU-Aufsichtsbehörde soll die Parteienfamilie ESN auf Werteverstöße überprüfen. Das EU-Parlament stimmte für eine Untersuchung der Gruppe, der auch die AfD angehört.

zeit.title: Soziale Medien: Social-Media-Verbot in Australien scheitert bereits an Altersabfrage
zeit.description: Das weltweit erste Social-Media-Verbot für Kinder in Australien zeigt offenbar wenig Wirkung. Eine neue Studie weckt nun weitere Zweifel an der Effektivität der Maßnahme.

zeit.title: Gewalt im Verkehr: Anklage fordert langjährige Haft in Prozess um getöteten Zugbegleiter
zeit.description: Anfang Februar wurde ein Zugbegleiter bei einer Kontrolle angegriffen und starb daraufhin. Für den mutmaßlichen Täter fordert die Staatsanwaltschaft zwölf Jahre Haft.

zeit.title: Verkehrsunfälle in Deutschland: Jeden Tag sterben acht Menschen auf Deutschlands Straßen
zeit.description: 2.832 Menschen sind im vergangenen Jahr bei Verkehrsunfällen gestorben. Häufigste Ursache für tödliche Unfälle ist eine überhöhte Geschwindigkeit.

zeit.title: Josef Hecken: »Da hat es halt ein paar Mal lauter geknallt«
zeit.description: Josef Hecken war einer der mächtigsten Männer im Gesundheitssystem – entschied mit, wofür Kassen zahlen, legte sich mit Ministern und Pharmafirmen an. Nun redet er offen.

nzz.title: Anschlag in Monaco: Die Tatverdächtige ist tot in der Ukraine aufgefunden worden
nzz.description: Drei Ukrainer sind in Monaco durch eine Paketbombe verletzt worden. Unter den Opfern hat sich der Unternehmer Wadim Jermolajew befunden. Seit Ende 2023 steht er auf der Sanktionsliste Kiews. Nun ist die Hauptverdächtige tot aufgefunden worden.

nzz.title: Bombenangriffe in Damaskus während Macrons Staatsbesuch: Frankreichs Präsident reist für eine riskante Visite nach Syrien
nzz.description: Für Ahmed al-Sharaa ist die erste Reise eines EU-Regierungschefs nach Syrien ein Coup. Macron erhofft sich, den französischen Einfluss in Nahost auszubauen.

nzz.title: EU-Parlament stimmt für Verfahren gegen AfD-Parteifamilie
nzz.description: Für die Dachorganisation der AfD auf EU-Ebene stehen Millionen-Fördermittel auf dem Spiel: Nach Hinweisen auf Grundwerte-Verstösse prüft das Europäische Parlament die Rechtsaussenpartei.

nzz.title: Symbol der Kriegszerstörung: Vögel in der Ukraine bauen ihre Nester aus Drohnenkabeln
nzz.description: Das Kiewer Kriegsmuseum hat ein neues Exponat in seiner Sammlung: ein Vogelnest, durchwebt von Glasfaserkabeln von Kampfdrohnen. Das tierische Kunstwerk ist ein Symbol für die Umweltkatastrophe in dem vom Krieg zerstörten Land.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Nato-Gipfel in Ankara: Bündnis bereitet sich auf mögliche Drohnenkriege vor +++ Bei Aufklärung wird nicht mehr auf US-Flugzeuge gesetzt
nzz.description: Die Verteidigungsallianz hat turbulente Monate hinter sich. In Ankara steht ein entscheidendes Treffen an. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Grossangriff auf Moskau, Schäden in russischen Regionen +++ Ukrainische Drohnen setzen Raffinerie in Sibirien in Brand
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten im Überblick.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Krise in Syrien: Explosionen in Damaskus während Macron-Besuch
nzz.description: Seit dem Sturz des langjährigen Machthabers Bashar al-Asad Ende 2024 erlebt Syrien ungewisse Zeiten. So zeigt sich zurzeit die Lage.

nzz.title: INTERAKTIV - Alle Angriffe und Rückeroberungen der letzten vier Kriegsjahre – klicken Sie sich durch unsere Karte
nzz.description: Seit vier Jahren kartografiert die NZZ täglich den Krieg in der Ukraine. Klicken Sie sich durch alle wichtigen Ereignisse im russischen Angriffskrieg.

nzz.title: DATENANALYSE - Wie beliebt ist Donald Trump?
nzz.description: Täglich aktualisierte Umfragewerte zeigen, wie die Amerikaner derzeit zur Amtsführung ihres Präsidenten stehen. Eine Übersicht in Grafiken.

nzz.title: INTERAKTIV - Spritpreise steigen nach Ende des Tankrabatts deutlich – die aktuellen Zahlen zur Energieversorgung in Deutschland
nzz.description: Wie wirken sich Energiewende und globale Krisen auf Strom- und Gaspreise aus? Hier gibt es jeden Tag die aktuellen Zahlen.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Emotionen und besondere Momente – Einblicke in die WM in Bildern
nzz.description: Drei Gastgeber, 48 Teilnehmer: Vom 11. Juni bis zum 19. Juli findet die Fussball-Weltmeisterschaft der Männer in Mexiko, Kanada und den USA statt. Einblicke in die WM in Bildern.

nzz.title: Donald Trumps Intervention nützt den USA nichts: Sie scheiden gegen Belgien im Achtelfinal aus
nzz.description: Der Einsatz des Stürmers Folarin Balogun bleibt wirkungslos – die Belgier gewinnen gegen ein schwaches amerikanisches Team 4:1.

nzz.title: Türkischer Antisemitismus: Erdogans Aussenminister bezeichnet Israel als «Problem der Menschheit»
nzz.description: Kurz vor dem Nato-Gipfel in der Türkei macht das Gastgeberland mit einer Äusserung von sich reden, die Israel das Existenzrecht abspricht – und den Juden die Zugehörigkeit zum Menschsein.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Fussball-WM 2026: Kolumbien muss auf einen Stürmer verzichten +++ Belgische Sticheleien gegen Trump
nzz.description: Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten zur Fussball-WM in Kanada, Mexiko und den USA.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Crans-Montana: Die Region Lombardei tritt als Zivilklägerin auf
nzz.description: In der Bar «Le Constellation» im Skiort Crans-Montana im Wallis ist es in der Neujahrsnacht zu einem verheerenden Brand gekommen. 41 Personen sind ums Leben gekommen. Die Ermittlungen laufen. Wir geben einen Überblick über den Stand der Dinge.

observador.title: Declaração ambiental para mina na Gudiña é obrigatória
observador.description: Comissão Europeia alerta para obrigatoriedade da avaliação de impacte ambiental transfronteiriça, que ainda não foi feita, sobre a exploração de volfrâmico, na Gudiña, Espanha, perto de Vinhais.

observador.title: Governo passa a fazer pagamento por conta a operadores
observador.description: Vai passar a ser feito um pagamento por conta em cada mês aos operadores de transporte pelas compensações do passe gratuito jovem, dando "maior previsibilidade" a este processo.

observador.title: Açores. Tolerância de ponto no Pico devido a festividades
observador.description: Trabalhadores da Administração Pública Regional dos Açores com tolerância de ponto no dia 6 de agosto pelas festas do Bom Jesus Milagroso.

observador.title: BE quer Portugal como líder nas áreas marinhas protegidas
observador.description: António Lima, deputado único do BE, afirma que "os Açores têm tudo a ganhar em liderar este processo". Partido vai apresentar propostas no parlamento regional para criar áreas marinhas protegidas.

observador.title: Ana Moura abre cartaz nas Festas de Peniche
observador.description: O cartaz conta ainda com concertos de Mizzy Miles, Deejay Telio, Sara Correia e Marisa Liz. Outros grupos e DJs vão animar as Festas de Peniche conhecida ainda pela famosa procissão marítima noturna.

observador.title: Aldeamento turístico e luxo em Tomar sem avaliação ambiental
observador.description: Quercus manifesta "muita apreensão" em relação à construção do "Amara Village", um aldeamento turístico de luxo nas margens da Albufeira de Castelo de Bode, ocupará 50 hectares.

observador.title: Suspeita do ataque com bomba no Mónaco encontrada morta
observador.description: Anastasia Berezovska conseguiu fugir do Mónaco após a explosão que visou um oligarca ucraniano alvo de sanções internacionais. Dois homens foram detidos por suspeitas de homicídio, um deles militar.

observador.title: O que fazer com tantos imigrantes em Portugal? — Debate
observador.description: Portugal tem mais de 1 milhão e meio de imigrantes e nova realidade trouxe novos desafios para serviços públicos e para partidos. Onde está ponto de equilíbrio nas políticas de imigração e integração?

observador.title: A primeira imagem de Mette-Marit depois do transplante
observador.description: A princesa da Noruega mostrou-se sorridente a assistir ao jogo da Noruega no sofá de casa, 20 dias depois do transplante de pulmão, mas a Casa Real nega que já tenha recebido alta do hospital.

observador.title: 12h. Acidente Cacém. Duas pessoas morrem atropeladas
observador.description: O acidente aconteceu cerca das 10 horas da manhã junto à estação ferroviária do Cacém. Ainda, o possível sucessor de Roberto Martínez na Seleção Nacional. E as declarações do secretário geral da NATO.

observador.title: ONG timorense alerta para subsídios encapotados a deputados
observador.description: A ONG sugere que falta de transparência "poderá comprometer a confiança pública no parlamento", recomendando ainda ao parlamento que peça um parecer jurídico independente.

observador.title: DGS reduz para nível 1 o risco do Plano Sazonal de Saúde
observador.description: Decisão é fundamentada nas previsões do IPMA, que prevê uma melhoria das condições meteorológicas com diminuição das temperaturas máximas e mínimas na generalidade do território.

observador.title: Calor: está a beber o suficiente?
observador.description: No verão, não basta beber “quando dá sede”: o corpo perde água antes de nos avisar. A Nutricionista Mariana Chaves esclarece

observador.title: Inteligência Artificial: é preciso agir antes da evidência
observador.description: Não encaramos a inteligência artificial como um setor isolado nem como uma moda tecnológica. Encaramo-la como um instrumento para modernizar o Estado e melhorar os serviços públicos

observador.title: China condena à morte funcionário que aceitou subornos
observador.description: Yang Youlin, um funcionário municipal de Nanjing, aceitou subornos ao longo de 30 anos. Foi condenado à morte por desvio de fundos, abuso de poder e branqueamento de capitais.

observador.title: Extremistas islâmicos reivindicam ataque em Moçambique
observador.description: Este é apenas um dos 11 ataques violentos registados nas duas primeiras semanas de julho na província de Cabo Delgado. Morreram 5 militares, um outro foi capturado e as suas armas foram apreendidas.

observador.title: Despiste na A25 provoca uma vítima mortal
observador.description: Um homem morreu na sequência de um despiste na A25, em Reigoso, na direção Viseu - Aveiro. Foram mobilizados 13 operacionais apoiados por 7 veículos. O alerta foi dado às 8h19.

observador.title: Prisão preventiva para suspeito de roubo de veículo em Nelas
observador.description: Medida de coação mais gravosa para homem detido em flagrante delito em Nelas. O suspeito terá praticado, no mesmo dia, um outro crime de roubo e um crime de ofensa à integridade física.

spiegel.title: Nato-Gipfel in Ankara: Mitgliedstaaten kündigen Milliarden-Deal für Aufklärungsflugzeuge an
spiegel.description: Kurz vor dem Nato-Gipfel in Ankara kündigen mehrere Mitgliedsstaaten den Kauf neuer Aufklärungsflugzeuge an. Nachdem die USA aus dem Projekt ausgestiegen ist, dürfte Deutschland den größten Anteil zahlen.

spiegel.title: Wandern im Urlaub: Alpenvereine bitten um Hilfe gegen Bettwanzen auf Berghütten
spiegel.description: Der Berg ruft, der Rücken juckt: In immer mehr Berghütten gibt es Probleme mit Wanzen. Drei deutschprachige Alpenvereine wollen jetzt gemeinsam gegen die Parasiten vorgehen – auch mit Plastiktüten.

spiegel.title: Drogen: Zahl der Drogentoten unter 30 steigt 2025 deutlich
spiegel.description: Die Zahl der jungen Menschen, die durch Drogen sterben, ist 2025 deutlich angestiegen. Der Drogenmarkt wird unübersichtlicher, neuere Substanzen wie synthetische Opioide oder Crack spielen eine immer größere Rolle.

spiegel.title: EU-Parlament stimmt für Prüfverfahren gegen rechtspopulistische ESN
spiegel.description: Wegen der Hinweise auf Grundwerte-Verstöße prüft das Europäische Parlament die rechtspopulistische Parteienfamilie Europa. Für die Dachorganisation der AfD stehen Millionen-Fördermittel auf dem Spiel.

spiegel.title: Brandenburg: Heino fordert nach AfD-Wahlwerbung mindestens 30.000 Euro
spiegel.description: Schwarzbraun wie die Haselnuss will Schlagersänger Heino auf keinen Fall sein. Nach ungewollter Wahlwerbung mit seinem Namen fordert er nun finanzielle Entschädigung von der AfD.

spiegel.title: Kondome: Tausende gefälschte Verhütungsmittel in Europa auf dem Markt
spiegel.description: Sicher ist sicher: In der EU gelten für Kondome hohe Qualitätsanforderungen. Nun wurden Tausende Verhütungsmittel aus China ohne Prüfung und mit falschem Logo angeboten.

spiegel.title: Ukraine: Hauptverdächtige nach Monaco-Anschlag offenbar nahe Kyjiw tot aufgefunden
spiegel.description: Eine 39-jährige Ukrainerin soll ein Sprengstoffattentat auf einen Oligarchen verübt haben – seitdem wird sie international gesucht. Nun soll sie einem Medienbericht zufolge tot in der Nähe von Kyjiw entdeckt worden sein.

spiegel.title: Australien: Mann nach Explosion im Krankenhaus – Saugroboter im Verdacht
spiegel.description: Ein junger Australier liegt mit schweren Brandverletzungen im Krankenhaus. Ein explodierter Saugroboter soll Berichten zufolge ein Feuer ausgelöst haben. Doch vieles ist unklar.

spiegel.title: Balkonkraftwerke: Viele Anlagen lassen sich laut Medienbericht leicht hacken
spiegel.description: Haben Sie eine Photovoltaikanlage mit einem Hoymiles-Wechselrichter? Ein Forscher hat eine Schwachstelle entdeckt, mit der er solche Systeme abschalten kann. Eine Lösung des Herstellers lässt noch auf sich warten.

spiegel.title: USA: Demokraten drängen Graham Platner wegen Vergewaltigungsvorwürfen zum Rückzug
spiegel.description: Graham Platner gilt als Hoffnungsträger der Demokraten bei den Senatswahlen im November. Immer wieder trübten Skandale seinen Erfolg. Nun sind neue Vorwürfe bekannt geworden, die sein politisches Ende bedeuten könnten.

spiegel.title: Gasreserve: Regierung plant strategische Vorräte, finanziert von Verbrauchern
spiegel.description: Schwarz-Rot geht eine staatliche Gasreserve für Krisenfälle an. Finanziert werden soll sie über eine Umlage auf die Gasverbraucher. Diese müssen sich auf deutlich höhere Kosten einstellen.

spiegel.title: Melissa George ist mit 49 Jahren noch einmal Mutter geworden
spiegel.description: Ihr Privatleben hält Melissa George größtenteils aus der Öffentlichkeit heraus. Aber alle paar Jahre stellt sie einen neuen Spross vor. Jetzt wieder.

spiegel.title: Frankfurt am Main: Spezialeinheiten stoppen offenbar Auftragsmörder mit Videobrille
spiegel.description: Womöglich in letzter Minute haben Sicherheitskräfte in der Main-Metropole fünf junge Männer gestoppt. Sie waren wohl kurz davor, mindestens einen Auftragsmord zu begehen. Die geplanten Taten sollten wohl aufgezeichnet werden.

spiegel.title: Finanzkrise der Gemeinden: Kommunen klagen über Rekordschulden – trotz beschlossener Entlastung
spiegel.description: Gewaltige Schuldenberge belasten Deutschlands Kommunen. Müssen die Lokalpolitiker jetzt ran an Steuern und Parkgebühren? Hier sagt die Kämmerin von Recklinghausen, wo sie Hebel sieht – und warum das Sondervermögen des Bundes nur wenig bringt.

spiegel.title: Rostock: Frau erlebte sexualisierte Gewalt durch ihren Physiotherapeuten - wie sie es schaffte, gegen ihn vorzugehen
spiegel.description: Sie werden begrapscht, bedrängt, vergewaltigt: Millionen Frauen in Deutschland erfahren sexualisierte Gewalt. Nur wenige reden darüber. Wissenschaftler erforschen, wie sich das Schweigen durchbrechen lässt – und Betroffene Hilfe finden.

spiegel.title: Heizungstausch: Regierung plant geringere Förderung für Wärmepumpen
spiegel.description: Schwarz-Rot will die staatliche Förderung für den Heizungstausch deutlich reduzieren. Die Höhe der förderfähigen Kosten soll sinken. Für niedrige Einkommen sollen Zuschüsse aber steigen.

spiegel.title: WM 2026 – Skandal um Balogun-Sperre: »Gianni Infantino sollte zurücktreten« – Pressestimmen
spiegel.description: Die internationale Presse ist einer Meinung: Donald Trump hat ein großartiges Turnier durch seine Einmischung in die Sperre von US-Spieler Folarin Balogun beschädigt. Besonders im Fokus: Fifa-Chef Infantino.

spiegel.title: WM 2026: Belgien verspottet Donald Trump und USA nach Sieg im Achtelfinale
spiegel.description: Nach der umstrittenen Aufhebung der Rotsperre für US-Stürmer Folarin Balogun reagiert Belgien mit Häme. Die Belgier stichelten nach dem 4:1-Sieg gegen die Gastgeber mit einem Tanz und einer spitzen Botschaft.

letemps.title: «La Suisse est devenue moins sociale»: les écarts de revenus se creusent depuis 2016, pointe l'USS

new-sci.description: An experiment that involved feeding a dead goat to a Komodo dragon as well as an analysis of thousands of ancient bones suggests that Homo floresiensis was neither a skilled hunter of big game nor a master of fire

new-sci.title: A volcano has erupted remnants of Earth's primordial magma ocean
new-sci.description: Earth was once covered by a global magma ocean, which later cooled and crystallised – now traces of this primordial event have been found in magma from a young volcano in the Indian Ocean

new-sci.title: Audacious mission to rescue NASA's falling telescope has launched
new-sci.description: NASA’s Swift space telescope is reaching the end of its two-decade run in orbit – unless a satellite launched on 3 July can give it a lifesaving boost

new-sci.title: Orangutan mothers seem to plan playdates for their offspring
new-sci.description: Female orangutans are generally solitary, but they travel more and eat less in an apparent effort to ensure their offspring have someone to play with

new-sci.title: This thoughtful book will make you look at the wonders of trees anew
new-sci.description: Aya Koda's Tree is an account of the late writer's visits to Japan's most famous, and ancient, trees. Featured in Wim Wenders's film Perfect Days, it is original and thought-provoking, says Rowan Hooper

new-sci.title: Stunning photos reveal the intricate beauty of fungi
new-sci.description: The vibrant colours and delicate details of New Zealand's fungi and slime moulds are documented in these images, taken from Jay Lichter's new book The Secret Life of Fungi

new-sci.title: Evocative photos of Canadian Arctic win New Scientist Editors Award
new-sci.description: Natalya Saprunova's photo series exploring coastal erosion and permafrost thaw across Inuvialuit territories in Canada has won the New Scientist Editors Award at the Earth Photo 2026 competition

phys-org.title: Bumblebees exposed to up to 7 times as much toxic metal as honeybees
phys-org.description: Bumblebees collect up to seven times the amount of toxic heavy metals as honeybees even when foraging in the same environment, new research from the University of Cambridge has found. Exposure to these metals can affect everything from their ability to forage for food to their ability to reproduce.

phys-org.title: Massive calving episode in Greenland may foreshadow more rapid ice sheet loss
phys-org.description: In November 2025, a study led by Adrien Wehrlé, a researcher in the Department of Geography at the University of Zürich, Switzerland, looked at the massive calving response of one of West Greenland's active glaciers, Sermeq Kujalleq in the Kangia icefjord (SKK), to the drainage of two surface lakes. Called supraglacial lakes, these are temporary meltwater ponds that form and accumulate in depressions or holes on the surface of glaciers and ice sheets.

phys-org.title: New beetle genus named after One Piece's Monkey D. Luffy, encompassing two new species
phys-org.description: A research team from the Natural History Museum of Denmark has published a compelling new study in insect taxonomy in the open-access journal ZooKeys, officially establishing a new genus of rove beetle: Luffy gen. nov. The inspiration for the name comes directly from Monkey D. Luffy, the iconic protagonist of the globally popular manga and anime One Piece.

phys-org.title: Why we need to consider city shapes to save energy, water, and the climate
phys-org.description: The world's future is in cities. It is estimated that by 2050, 7 out of 10 people will live in urban areas (although a recent CSH study suggests that the growth of large cities may be less dramatic than current projections indicate, it still points to continued and substantial urban growth).

phys-org.title: Chemical control dominates global fight against invasive alien plants
phys-org.description: Efforts to manage invasive alien plant species in forests could be held back by a continued reliance on chemical methods, according to a new study. Research led by Lizzie Keen, a postgraduate researcher at Newcastle University's School of Natural and Environmental Sciences, shows that chemical methods remain the dominant approach worldwide, despite growing recognition of the need for more sustainable management options.

phys-org.title: 'Cosmic wallflowers' may hold the key to the origin of globular clusters
phys-org.description: Astronomers using computer simulations have investigated whether a class of star clusters nicknamed "cosmic wallflowers" could be the long-sought ancestors of the globular clusters we see orbiting galaxies today. Their paper, posted to the arXiv preprint server on June 25, suggests that where a cluster is born and how fast it spins may determine its fate.

phys-org.title: It's disturbingly easy to trick AI into seeing aliens, say researchers
phys-org.description: Are we alone in the universe? Consider mysterious "extraterrestrial" radio signals. Unexplained gases on other planets. Things mistaken for UFOs.

phys-org.title: EV-SELEX speeds GPCR drug discovery by capturing receptor-bound DNA aptamers
phys-org.description: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) are the most abundantly expressed proteins in the human body, regulating diverse physiological processes ranging from pain perception to hormone signaling. Owing to their central roles in health and disease, GPCRs are the targets of a majority of new drugs under development. Despite their importance, discovering drug candidates that bind to GPCRs with high affinity and specificity remains a major challenge, slowing the development of safer therapeutics.

phys-org.title: Bulk ferromagnetic quasicrystals emerge without rapid quenching, unlocking stable magnetic studies
phys-org.description: Ferromagnetism has long been studied in a wide range of periodic crystals and amorphous materials. In quasicrystals (QCs), which possess long-range quasiperiodic order and unconventional rotational symmetries, such as 10-fold symmetry, ferromagnetism remained elusive until recently, when it was finally realized in gold (Au)-based icosahedral QCs. These discoveries establish QCs as a third platform for magnetism beyond periodic crystals and amorphous materials.

phys-org.title: Scientists just measured the smallest possible contacts for future computer chips
phys-org.description: The rise of AI has created an almost insatiable appetite for computing power. Training and running AI systems requires vast numbers of transistors, and engineers are now racing to pack more of them onto every chip. With their existing designs, however, silicon transistors are rapidly running up against physical limits on how small they can get.

phys-org.title: Bacteria discovered with the ability to jettison cells as a survival mechanism
phys-org.description: Popular science fiction is no stranger to escape-pod scenarios, typically featuring characters who narrowly avoid their demise by jettisoning from a spaceship—think R2-D2 and C-3PO shooting away from a rebel spaceship in the opening of Star Wars: A New Hope. Biologists at the University of California San Diego have found that communities of bacteria feature a similar ejection capability.

phys-org.title: How proximity steals energy from nanoresonators
phys-org.description: Nanomechanical resonators are miniature vibrating structures on chips that oscillate at frequencies ranging from a few kilohertz to gigahertz. They are used as ultrasensitive detectors of mass and force, temperature and pressure, and as components in radio frequency filters and on-chip clocks. Modern, state-of-the-art resonators are also used to create quantum states of macroscopic objects and test fundamental physics.

phys-org.title: Raptorial insect forelegs evolved repeatedly but never converged on one winning design
phys-org.description: The evolutionary paths that created snatching forelimbs in insects multiple times moved in a similar direction but didn't end at a single solution. Kobe University research is pioneering a study of how organs with similar functions evolve, providing a new analytical approach to identify evolutionary dynamics quantitatively.

phys-org.title: Ancient rocks reveal how water reshaped Earth's interior 3.1 billion years ago
phys-org.description: Geologists studying some of the planet's oldest volcanic rocks have uncovered new evidence that water was playing a major role in shaping Earth's interior and driving volcanic activity more than 3 billion years ago.

phys-org.title: Death toll from China storms rises to 15, hundreds injured
phys-org.description: The death toll from devastating storms in parts of China rose to 15 on Tuesday, with hundreds more injured and tens of thousands evacuated, state media reported, as President Xi Jinping urged "all-out" rescue efforts.

phys-org.title: Making scents of cannabis: How cannabis cultivar and preparation methods influence aroma
phys-org.description: Ongoing research reveals how the aroma of cannabis is influenced not only by the chosen cultivar, but also by different drying and storage methods. Through a combination of high-resolution chromatography and human-perception aroma assessments, this project provides detailed insights into the impact of preparation and transportation on cannabis chemistry and how humans perceive and interpret its aromas.

phys-org.title: New biobased polymers exhibit excellent tensile properties beyond polyolefins
phys-org.description: The research group of Professor Kotohiro Nomura, Tokyo Metropolitan University, in cooperation with the research groups of Senior Researcher Hiroshi Hirano and Director Seiji Higashi of the Osaka Research Institute of Industrial Science and Technology, and Associate Professor Hiroki Takeshita of The University of Shiga Prefecture, has developed biobased poly(ester amide)s from inedible biorenewables that can be easily chemically recycled and exhibit better mechanical (tensile) properties in film

phys-org.title: Newly discovered mineral named for researcher Tyler Spano
phys-org.description: Tyler Spano's impact on the field of mineralogy is anything but small. So when a newly discovered mineral, modest in size but significant in meaning, was named spanoite in her honor, it became a fitting tribute to her contributions to the field.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

proj-syn.title: Just Say No to Remote Work
proj-syn.description: Even during the immediate post-pandemic period, when evidence on the labor-market effects of remote work was scant, there was a strong case to be made for going into the office, especially for younger workers. And now, multiple new studies have vindicated this intuition.

proj-syn.title: There Is Only One Acceptable Path for Designer Babies
proj-syn.description: Genetic-engineering tools with which to design one's progeny already exist, and they are being made even more potent with AI—at least for those who can afford such services. In the absence of policy interventions, we will be hurtling toward a tiered society in which economic privileges become biological advantages.

proj-syn.title: The Democratic Turkey NATO Needs
proj-syn.description: At NATO's upcoming summit in Ankara, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan will seek to portray his country as stable, confident, and essential to Western security. But only the last one is true, which is why the restoration of democracy in Turkey is more than a domestic concern.

proj-syn.title: The World Cup as It Should Be
proj-syn.description: While Donald Trump was widely expected to lord over this year’s World Cup, which the United States is co-hosting with Mexico and Canada, it has turned out not to be his scene. National teams populated with immigrants, and small-town America’s embrace of the event, go against everything Trump’s MAGA movement stands for.

proj-syn.title: The Real Threat to NATO
proj-syn.description: The greatest challenge to NATO comes not from its adversaries but from within. As its leaders gather in Ankara on July 7-8, they should focus less on military capabilities than on reinvigorating the alliance's founding strategic philosophy, centered on democratic legitimacy, human rights, and the rule of law.

proj-syn.title: How the EU Can Lead the Rest of the West
proj-syn.description: While Europe is not just another middle power, nor is it a great power with sufficient economic, military, and geopolitical clout to dictate terms on the global stage. Instead, Europe is the ideal candidate to convene and lead a group of like-minded middle powers, not as a US-style hegemon, but as a first among equals.

proj-syn.title: Europe Must Face the World on Its Own
proj-syn.description: Under pressure from Russian aggression—which has reached its full expression in the ongoing war against Ukraine—and an increasingly hostile US administration, Europe urgently needs to make progress toward a defense union. But that will require Franco-German leadership of the kind that is not yet on offer.

proj-syn.title: How Safe Are Today’s Blockbuster Tech Stocks?
proj-syn.description: Today’s wave of mega-IPOs has unleashed a wave of analogies to past booms. While no analogy is perfect, an especially apposite—and sobering—case may be what followed Nippon Telegraph and Telephone’s IPO in February 1987.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s AI Dolce Vita?
proj-syn.description: Glacial growth, aging welfare states, and a shortage of centrist leaders suggest Europe faces a major debt crisis in the years ahead. But its emphasis on leisure over work could become a decisive advantage, positioning the continent as the leading model for thriving in an age of AI-driven abundance.

proj-syn.title: The Putin Escalation Risk
proj-syn.description: If Ukraine can continue to disrupt Crimea, strike more targets in the heart of Russia, frustrate Russia’s frontline forces, and pile more pressure on Russia’s hobbled economy, President Vladimir Putin will feel increasingly cornered. The temptation to escape his predicament through a game-changing attack will grow stronger.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s New German Question
proj-syn.description: Without a EU-level framework capable of turning resources into scale, the bloc’s defense capabilities will remain limited, no matter how much member countries spends. If Germany, in particular, insists on going it alone, Europe could remain fully dependent on the US for key assets.

proj-syn.title: From the American Revolution to Universal Suffrage
proj-syn.description: Britain’s attempt to crush the American Revolution exposed a constitutional crisis at the heart of its empire. One English statesman saw in it proof that only broader suffrage could check royal power, tame corruption, and ensure that imperial rule remained compatible with liberty.

proj-syn.title: 250 Years of American State Capitalism
proj-syn.description: While the prevailing economic narrative in the United States has often extolled free markets, policymaking itself has always been more pragmatic. From its very founding, the US has had a hybrid model in which the state directs, subsidizes, and occasionally bails out private enterprise in the service of national priorities.

proj-syn.title: Three Essentials of a More Equal World Order
proj-syn.description: A growing awareness of the inequities embedded in the world order has prompted calls for reform. Building a multilateral system that serves the global majority will require redesigning the international financial architecture, especially in relation to sovereign debt and corporate taxation.

proj-syn.title: The US as the World’s Robber Baron
proj-syn.description: Like the Gilded Age robber barons, the United States under President Donald Trump is using trade policy to benefit itself at the expense of all other countries. But now that administration surrogates are openly acknowledging the strategy, all other major trading powers will surely respond accordingly.

proj-syn.title: A Democratic Opening for Azerbaijan
proj-syn.description: With Armenia's recent elections likely to usher in an era of greater stability—and less Russian influence—in the South Caucasus, neighboring Azerbaijan is well-positioned to deepen cooperation with the US and Europe. But without appropriate conditions, new strategic partnerships with the West could fail to deliver for Azerbaijanis.

proj-syn.title: The Mismeasure of Europe’s Economy
proj-syn.description: While Nobel laureate economists Paul Krugman and Philippe Aghion disagree over how to measure Europe’s productivity gap with the United States, both overlook the value of its accumulated assets. That blind spot obscures the real story: Europe is living off a remarkable inheritance it has yet to convert into new growth.

proj-syn.title: NATO Needs a Defense Market
proj-syn.description: To convert NATO members' resources into military capabilities, setting defense as a strategic priority, increasing spending, and improving procurement systems are all steps in the right direction. But member countries will need to expand their industrial capacity—and that requires much more.
